chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Jabir who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The 'ghayrah' (sense of honour/ jealousy) of women is envy, and envy is the root of disbelief. Indeed, when women feel ghayrah, they become angry, and when they are angry, they disbelieve, except for the Muslim women among them.

key_terms.غَيْرَةُ: Sense of honour, jealousy, or protective zeal

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between women's ghayrah, anger, and disbelief according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links women's 'ghayrah' (sense of honor/jealousy) to 'hasad' (envy), identifying it as the root of 'kufr' (disbelief). He explains that this emotional state leads to anger, which can result in a temporary lapse into disbelief, except for 'al-Muslimat'—those whose faith remains steadfast and submissive to God despite their emotions. This hadith highlights the distinction between the natural emotional response of jealousy and the spiritual state of true submission in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Yusuf Bin Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Jabir who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ‘الْغَيْرَةُ’ (sense of honour) of the women is the envy, and the evil is the root of the disbelief. The women, when they express الْغَيْرَةُ, they get angry, and when they are angry, they commit disbelief, except for the submissive ones from them’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Yusuf ibn Hammad from those whom he has mentioned from Jabir who has said the following: “

Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Pride of women is jealousy and jealousy is the root of disbelief. When women become jealous they become angry and when they become angry they disbelieve except the Muslim ones among them.’”
